changes.current_line: Every payout reconciles automatically to its transactions and your ERP.
changes.change: For finance-led buyers, lead with this line and use their words: Know where every deposit is, and close month-end without 'a week of archaeology.' Say 'the deposits', not payouts or payments.
changes.why: Reconciliation was the only message that got a reaction, strong enough that the CFO said 'go back', and she described it as an outcome ('I just want to know where my money is') in words like 'the deposits', never 'payments'.

changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: Send us one month of your statements and we'll price what manual deposit matching and unmatched-deposit write-offs cost you, built from your own data and your own costs.
changes.why: The deal turned when the value case was built from the customer's own statements and hours, and the CFO accepted it as 'my number, not yours', which an external study cannot offer.

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: For finance-led buyers with no in-house build team and no cross-border need, stop opening the first-call deck with this line, and with M2 'Built for developers: launch payments fast with our APIs, docs and sandbox.' Open on M9 instead.
changes.why: The standard opener landed in 'Silence' with a buyer whose IT team 'aren't building anything', and 'Nobody said 'infrastructure.''

changes.current_line: Support plans with tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage.
changes.change: Against bank-bundled incumbents: You'll get a named contact and always know who your person is. Don't lead with rates.
changes.why: The incumbent's only known move was a rate offer the CFO rejected ('I didn't ask about my rates.'), and her one new question afterwards was whether she'd get a named contact, which response-time tiers don't answer.
